today_summary: GCM26 marked $4,476 on the 2026-09-07 snapshot, −$63 (−1.39%) from Friday's $4,539, finishing pinned $24 beneath the $4,500 call wall — 11,108 contracts, the largest live-strike concentration in the chain. ATM IV lifted to 23.69%, a 5-session high, putting the 1σ daily move at $66.80 (1.49%). The chain stays structurally call-heavy at 0.40 P/C OI (201,767 calls vs 79,770 puts), but that skew is legacy far-OTM inventory: the $5,500 line alone holds 12,715 calls and drags reported max pain to $5,650, 26% above spot and non-operative as a magnet. five_day_thesis: Spot has round-tripped to nowhere — $4,481 on 09-01 to $4,476 on 09-07, a net −$4.90 (−0.11%) that conceals a $143 swing through $4,396 and $4,539. What changed is the price of that chop: ATM IV climbed 22.69% → 23.69% (+1.0pp), so the market is paying more for the same net displacement and realized-versus-implied is deteriorating for premium buyers. Max pain compressed $5,900 → $5,650 (−$250) and the call wall collapsed $8,000 → $6,000 on 09-02 and has not moved in four sessions — far-dated upside inventory is being written down rather than rolled higher. Dealer gamma held positive all five days but the ±$200 window total oscillated 543 → 441 → 495 → 712 → 601, peaking on Friday's $4,539 rally and bleeding off on the retrace, so the stabilizing bid is thinning at the top of the range. The put wall has not left $3,500 (5,732 contracts) for the entire window, meaning there is no OI-defined floor anywhere near spot — the nearest real put support is $4,300 with just 3,315 contracts.
